messages:
sarah_support: FYI — ACME (org_id=9987) flagged that their Console daily usage charts show ~5% less tokens compared to the CSV billing export for 2026-03-08..2026-03-14. They say the chart boundary looks shifted (cutting days at 07:00 UTC). Screenshot: https://files.redwood/acme/chart-vs-csv.png

ben_engineer: Thanks. Do we know org timezone and which user exported the CSV? Could be mixing account vs org tz.

sarah_support: Org timezone is America/Los_Angeles (PST/PDT). CSV was downloaded from Billing > Usage CSV by jane@acme on 2026-03-15. Repro steps they gave: 1) View daily chart (Console -> Usage -> Daily) 2) Download CSV (Billing -> Exports -> last 7d) 3) Compare totals — chart sums are lower.

lina_product: Noted. We recently changed the chart timezone dropdown to respect viewer preference, but exports always use org timezone. Might be a mismatch.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: web-frontend@release-2026-03-12 (shard: us-west) — metric-aggregation service unchanged.

ben_engineer: Sharing quick DB query I used to inspect the aggregator:
```sql
-- aggregation for daily totals (simplified)
SELECT org_id,
       date_trunc('day', recorded_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS day_utc,
       sum(tokens) AS tokens_utc
FROM usage_events
WHERE org_id = 9987
  AND recorded_at >= '2026-03-08'::timestamptz
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 2;
```
If UI is applying viewer timezone before date_trunc (or applying account_tz), you'll get different buckets.

sarah_support: I also pulled the CSV in both my account (Europe/London) and using a test admin (America/Los_Angeles). The CSV numbers are identical (org-level export), but the chart viewed as a London user shows totals split differently.

ben_engineer: That nails it — chart is honoring viewer timezone (probably `user_tz`) when building the histogram, while CSV and billing pipelines use `org_tz` for rollup. That mismatch will create cross-boundary splits especially around DST change.

lina_product: Is this a regression? Do we have a ticket?

escalation-bot: Created ticket INF-1249: "Daily usage chart buckets by viewer tz, exports use org tz leading to mismatched totals". Priority: P1 for customer impact. Linked: https://tracker.redwood/INF-1249

ben_engineer: Quick mitigation options:
- Short term: Add a note in UI explaining charts respect viewer timezone and exports use org timezone (low-effort).
- Medium: Make chart use org timezone by default for org admins, or provide toggle (preferred UX).
- Hotfix: If urgent for ACME, force chart to use org_tz for that org id until a permanent fix.

oncall_mike: I'm oncall and taking this. Can you dump a sample of raw timestamps around the boundary? I want to confirm DST impact and whether any aggregator job truncated using `AT TIME ZONE account_tz` anywhere. ETA 2 hours.

ben_engineer: Pushed a quick query and pasted 10 raw events near boundary to the ticket. Example rows show recorded_at timestamps crossing midnight local time but early morning UTC (07:00).

sarah_support: Customer ok with short-term mitigation (toggle or note). They're asking for a hotfix if it's an easy switch. I'll keep them updated and link the ticket. :thumbsup:

oncall_mike: Thanks — marking INF-1249 P1, will follow up in the ticket with root cause and plan. If we need a hotfix, I'll coordinate with releases.
